translations.text: Bless my speech, O Christ, O Lord of the seven heavens! May the gift of devotion be given to me, O King of the bright sun!
O bright sun that lights up heaven with the greatness of holiness, O King who rules the angels, O Lord of mankind!
O Lord of mankind, O righteous King, truly good, may every blessing come to me for praising your royal host.
It is your royal host I praise, for you are my sovereign; I have set my mind on praying to them continually.
I pray them for a favour: may what I have undertaken protect me, the fair people of shining colour, the royal host I have commemorated.
I have commemorated the royal host around the King above the clouds, some above bright days, some beneath swift tears [?].
May my course prosper [?], for I am wretched and sorrowful; by the commands of this King this host ran a course that succeeded.
They cut roads that were not easy for the foolish; before coming to the King they endured sufferings.
They were struck [?] before hosts, though they were in their strength [?]; they were crushed in assemblies, they were slain before kings.
They were pierced with points, they were cut into pieces, they were burned over fires on red-hot plates.
They were thrown to beasts by men without honour; they were scourged, a hard course, through furnaces of fire.
They were brought out of prisons to crosses to be tormented [?], the host driving them on after flaying them with their blades.
They welcomed every death out of their very great strength [?]; they used to endure glorious, great bloodshed from tortures beforehand.
All of them endured this lamentation [?], many deeds of valour, to truly earn the thanks of Jesus, son of Mary.
Woe to everyone who slew them, who dared to wound them! After their brief toil they live as long as he lives.
The great kings of the heathen are forever wailing in burning; the hosts of Jesus, without loss, are joyful after victory.
The band by whom they were slain, for all the greatness of their harshness, their splendour has perished, their strongholds are desolate.
It is they who after their toils have reached the kingdom; their burial grounds, not hidden away, are meeting-places of thousands.
The soldiers who crucified them, though they were strong in battle, their torments are great [?], their graves are unknown.
Not so the soldiers of Jesus: they have reached a shining dwelling; after them their devout bodies lie in shrines of gleaming gold.
Christ's royal host is mighty before the throngs [?] after their bloodshed; the kings of the world, after their desires, have utterly vanished from their seats.
Herod and Pilate, under whom our Lord suffered: their powers have been destroyed, their torments last forever.
Jesus, though he was crucified, our Lord, our champion, who created every element, is the perfect King who has risen.
Though ruddy Nebuchadnezzar was king of the world, mighty of grasp [?], when he died along with his household his dignity was cut off.
Not so old Paul the monk, from his gloomy desert: by his holy name, with great grace, every joyful host is blessed.
Though a sword struck down mighty John the Baptist, because he was exalted he was made king in the kingdom of God.
Herod with his queen, by whom he was slain, with a great host of cries [?], did not win (a hard course) either earth or holy [?] heaven.
Every synod proclaims the holy name of Peter the apostle; a believer does not think it worthy to call on the name of Nero.
Nero's grave is not known; that is fitting, for he was no believer [?]. The world, with its multitude of people, honours the little tomb of Peter.
Nero has a chief seat in the forefront of torment [?]; Paul the apostle, a lofty pillar, has reached the plains of heaven.
Nero's dignity has passed away; it is long since then. The name of Paul, lasting his election, is in full flood.
Though Pilate's queen was proud in her fortress of down [?], her splendour has been cut off since she went into the place of earth.
Not so Mary the Virgin: dear is her strong fortress. Of the seed of Adam, a lofty border [?], great is her glory among the host of angels.
Though many and beautiful were the children of wrathful Decius, whom we do not love, it is not known that the name of any one of them is great on earth.
Not so Cyricus the little boy: his great story has been spread abroad. Fair was the cry of his battle; it has filled the towns of the world.
Let all our mind be on God's people, and let us not conceal it. The prologue we offer is profitable if we put it to the test.
The power of the world is a lie to everyone who has sense; all true power is great love for the Son of Mary.
Though the kings of the world whose fortresses you see are great, the humble soldiers of Jesus are a hundred hundred times nobler.
Though they are lowly before men, with the sound of their cries they will be high above the citadel of the kingdom for ever and ever.
The wretched world in which we are, its kingship is fleeting; the King who rules the angels is Lord of every land.
Even the land in which we are has rich places of resort [?]; by the might of God (a famous sound) there is in it a fortress that has been preached [?].
The mighty stronghold of Tara has perished with the death of its princes; with a multitude of venerable choirs, great Armagh endures.
The pride of very valiant Lóegaire has been quenched; great the decline [?]. The name of Patrick, splendid and famous, is ever increasing.
The faith has increased; it will endure until Doomsday. The guilty heathens are carried off; their forts are not inhabited.
The fort of Cruachan has passed away along with Ailill, a victorious offspring; fair is the dignity, above princes, in the city of Clonmacnoise.
Lasting, melodious choirs surround Ciarán, if you speak of it [?], with the victorious clamour of great Clonmacnoise.
Nothing will be more your own than the love of God, if you have practised it, and the worship of the King of the clouds; because of it you will not be sorrowful.
The proud stronghold of Ailenn has perished with its warlike host; great is victorious Brigit, and fair is her thronged cemetery.
The stronghold of Emain has melted away; only its stones remain. The Rome of the western world is thronged Glendalough.
The radiant, splendid lamp of Ferns, mighty its flame, lives on; the proud throng of the fort of Bécc son of Eógan does not survive.
Why do you not all consider the judgments of the same King? Bécc son of Éogan does not live on; Áed son of Sétna lives on.
The old cities of the heathen, around which long possession [?] was spread, are deserted and without worship, like Lugaid's site (Lathrach Lugdach).
The little places that were settled by twos and threes are now Romes with assemblies, with hundreds, with thousands.
Heathendom has been destroyed, though it was splendid and widespread; the kingdom of God the Father has filled heaven, earth and sea.
We have something nearer to our eyes, a goodly psalm [?], from the might of God, swift its joy [?], today at the end of the world.
Visiting the tombs of fierce, red, choice Donnchad or victorious Bran of the Barrow does not take from me the anxiety of my weakness.
Máel Rúain, after his short time [?], the great sun south of Mag Mide: at his grave, in purity, the sigh of every heart is healed.
The Lord is just [?], though his flocks are counted [?]; his enemies are forever ebbing away, his champions forever live on.
The illustrious kings have been snuffed out; the Domnalls have been struck down; the Ciaráns have been crowned; the Cronáns have been magnified.
The great hills of evil have been cut down with spear-points, while the valleys have been made into mountain slopes.
Though we have to march out to battle against the bold Devil, for our protection, a high pillar, the same Christ lives on.
Though the kings of the earth are proud, in garments of greater brightness, they will die after their fullness [?]; each goes before another.
The gentle, dutiful King, Jesus above the flooding wave, since he was born of Mary, lives on after them all.
The might of the Devil with his ugly black host has been crushed [?]; the might of the champion of our queen [?] lives forever in wholeness [?].
Whoever runs [?] under his diadem will come to his portion, for he is not timid [?]; nothing will be refused there.
Let our resolve be firm, striving toward what is most fitting [?], for this is the noblest thing: let us all love Jesus.
O Jesus, I pray you for the sake of these hosts: by your will is this great good; I have made their reckoning.
I have done it according to your will, O King of populous Zion: may I live forever with your royal company in the everlasting, victorious kingdom!
May I live at your hand in the kingdom where you are! The blessing of every assembly [?] be upon your dignity, O Jesus!
O Jesus, I have striven to make your royal company known, in the order in which they went to you to cloudy heaven!
O Christ, though one may hear otherwise [?], there is no day in the year on which the other world has not received a company.
It is clear, O Lord, O King by whom princes are counted: we will name without fault the noble candles of every day.
We will set out our little book for anyone who seeks them; we will go without failing through every straight course of the year.
Let the body of our composition be arranged [?] so that it is not obscure: as many fair chapters as there are days in the year.
So that your mind will not be in confusion [?] through toil, every chapter will name without fault the feast of each day.
The days of the great month that this lasting sun runs through: on this splendid hosting we shall not break off this cry.
Nones and Ides, a course of calends [?] truly; on your margin, brightly, will be the lines.
Read them by days in your careful little books; read them line by line carefully for the feasts.
Unless you understand in this way the order that is in our lays, I proclaim you before assemblies among blind-witted people.
Let us make an increase of knowledge for the understanding with zeal: every chapter without fault will name the feast of each day.
As for the days of the solar month, its chanting [?] does not help me for my lay, which is not sluggish, except for twice six fair calends.
From one calend to the next nothing helps me along the ways except three hundred and sixty-five noble chapters.
In seeking the feast of mighty radiance, like a tower, attend carefully and diligently to the order of the chapters.
The order of the chapters with their careful lays is the order, line by line, that is followed for the feasts.
The holy Ruler of the elements, Christ, son of holy Mary, beloved Jesus, the pillar, submitted [?] before the race of men.
Before the race of eloquent men the pre-eminent King submitted [?]: he went under the Law, a lofty ordinance, Christ, on the calends of January.
Esodir [?] the bishop, abbot of a lofty church; splendid Manchéne of Airec; Scothíne, diadem of Mairg.
The great martyrdom of Rodon [?] with his clergy, fair moon; Fintan with the excellence of nobility; steadfast Findlug of Dún Blésce.
The holy death of Aquilinus with a band that was strong; in the blood of Christ, through their bodies, they won [?] their garments.
The summoning of the venerable Simeon to Christ, a form that has made us bright [?]; she was a fair sun, a new champion, Ciar, daughter of Dub Réa.
A grace with the King, a glorious choice, Julian, a cliff of purity; it should not be violated, a sound joy, the great baptism of Mary's Son.
The martyrdom of Lucian with a great host that was most steadfast [?]; I have commemorated what is nobler, the beginning of Jesus's Lent.
The death of Egemon [?], a bishop of lofty chastity [?]; Ercnat the virgin, a splendid inheritance; modest Nechtan of Scotland.
Beautiful pledges with purity before the face of the King you have spoken of [?]: divine, ardent Fáelán; Felix, Find, Vitalis.
We beseech their intercession that no evil lot may befall us: holy Mílit of the fair helmet; Diarmait of Inis Clothrann.
The crucifixion of the martyr Peter with his host full of valour. Out of Egypt, a splendid joy, came the great Son of Mary.
The great martyrdom of Muscentius [?] with his fair, numerous clergy; Laidcenn son of Baíth Bannach, who set forth [?] the mysteries of Christ.
Their blessing will be with us, a strong prayer without blemish: famous, gentle Sulpicius; Hilary, abbot of Poitiers.
The passion of Glycerius the deacon, who was loving towards our Lord; the venerable one of Nola, holy and famous Felix; fair, prosperous Fland.
She overcame much sharp sickness, she loved much heavy fasting, the bright sun of the women of Munster, Íte of Cluain Credal.
The devout ones on the feast of Fursa, who have hoped for the kingdom: nine thousand (what a great victory!) beyond twenty great thousands.
Let us praise them often, because they are not harsh: the people who suffered without guilt, on the feast of Antony the monk.
The honouring of Peter the apostle in Rome, a most exalted saying, together with the noblest feast, the great death of the mother of Jesus.
The death of Maris and Martha, a married couple who nurture us, together with the feast of old Paul, fair and splendid, with its nobleness.
Splendid are the four whom I join together on one feast, which is the holiest: Mo Laca, Mo Écu, Sebastian and Óenu.
May they be united in protecting me as I go to my King, a most exalted course: Fuinche, a nobler service, and Agnes, daughter of Jesus.
The death of Comgall's daughters, Colmán moccu Béognae, Valerius without disgrace, and Felix, who received a melodious visit.
The passion of Severianus, with Clement, whom I set together. May they protect us as we go to the King, with their bold host [?].
For my soul and for my poor body may Babylas, a glow of full gold, with his three little ones, be a wall against every bewilderment [?].
Its day is not feeble, a feast on which shouts are raised: a swarm went to Christ, and Paul was brought to baptism.
Mighty is their lamp with the King who looks upon us [?]: a host slain after famine, together with the passion of Polycarp.
Muirgen loved boasts [?], a wonderful birth with victories. Agnes, with ten virgins, carried off a pure victory before kings.
With Accobrán the [?], the splendid passion of eight virgins. A great host of Messorianus won victory with uprightness.
The splendid bishops I have named are Hippolytus, Paul, Gildas and Constantine. May they protect us for our forgiveness [?].
A hundred and fifty martyrs, a martyrdom that opened a great door [?]. May Enán of Ross, a bright star, protect us against a multitude of attacks!
Name Áed of Ferns, the very mighty, and Máel Anfaid, a name of renown [?]. Together with the very great Brigit, they set a fair crown on the host of January.
The calends of February honour a shower of great, very bright martyrs, and Brigit, fair, strong and renowned, the chaste head of the nuns of Ireland.
The reception of Mary's Son in the Temple, certain and splendid; a great and gentle host of martyrs, together with the ardent Findech of Dorn.
May a fair, modest host come to us with fullness at all times, against every misery: Felix and Symphronius.
I have known Fronius and Magnus, and Gelasius; Germanus, the noble martyr; and Cuannae, faithful and devout.
Agatha's body was crucified, the champion with purity. With Jesus, in brightness, she has great good for it.
Andrew, whose dignity is high; Bishop Mel, a diadem of kingship; and Lucia, splendid, whom thousands could not move.
Mellán of the noble Island of Maccu Cuinn, who nurtures us; Lommán of Loch Uair, a lamp of strength and a high pillar.
The splendid descendant of the poet [?], whose speech was about Christ; Fiachra was a manly man, the famous abbot of Irard.
Mo Chúaróc of wisdom, a saint who did not endure disgrace; Cáirech Dergan the godly; and Bishop Rónán the kingly.
A shining gem, a victorious birth, a glow of gold, the brightness of splendour: holy Crónán without blemish, bright sun of Glas Mór.
My Gobnat of pure goodness, for love of God she was rich in treasures [?]. It is good to him [?] that I constantly call on beloved Bishop Étchén.
With Bishop Simplex a tried, chief host was cut down; Damian, a soldier, a diadem of martyrdom, with a fair band of crucified youths.
In a little coracle, from the east over the bright-coloured sea, Modomnóc brought (a mighty cry) the victorious stock of the bees of Ireland.
In the contest [?] of Valentinus, Marcellus was torn apart; in the kingdom of Christ eighty fair champions were planted.
Fair is the Sunday celebration on the feast of warlike Berach, with the passion of a mighty host, the victory of the Son of God over his enemy.
For the virgin Juliana, a splendid name, a cloud to the edge [?]; with the shield of the story of her protection, the Devil submitted to being fettered [?].
Let everyone proclaim as far as the great sea the feast of Cormac of pure goodness, together with the feast of watchful Fintan of great Cluain Ednech.
Holy Colmán, whom they used to call Mo Liba, died on the fair and holy feast of Rutulus and Silvanus.
Name, with the passion of Publius, the passion of Marcellus, a victorious diadem; great, wealthy Baíthíne, the shining son of Cúanu.
Gaius the bishop, his passion is not hidden; around him were slaughtered (a grievous tale) thirty strong, prudent men.
The calling of Fintan of Corach, after contempt of the world, on the fair and joyful feast of Verulus and Jucundus.
In Antioch was Peter's ordination, learning declares; the birth of Laurence, full of response [?], with the shining feast of Thecla.
Matthias the apostle, who suffered torments for Christ: may he protect us to the kingdom, with everyone who submits to him.
With the passion of Lucianus, a priest surely crucified; the abbot of Iona, splendid in knowledge, excellent Cummíne Find.
The head of Paul the apostle, the splendid, faithful champion, was found on the feast of the fettered [?] man, strong, fasting Teolis.
The calling of Alexander into the dwelling of the saints; on one festival, a full fire, the birth of the Tarcelli [?].
With the passion of Abundius (if I have dared to put it in lays [?]), the feast of Comgan without contempt, the finding of the head of John.
On the feast of Sillán of Bangor, ten holy, shapely virgins, together with the passion of a manly host, complete the company of February.
On the calends of the month of March, they are not too great to be prayed to: Senán, Moinenn, Moses, David of Cell Muni.
If feasts are remembered: on the passion of Lucilla, the birth of Old Paul (salvation to him), the fair feast of Fergna of Iona.
On the passion of Florianus is the feast of two foremost [?] shining gems: Céle Críst (a fair command [?]) and Mo Macru son of Senán.
Proclaim the passion of the bishop in Rome, kingly and radiant, with a vast angelic host: Lucius, a gleaming light.
Their fame leapt, not silently, over the eastern sea: kingly, ruddy Carthach, and Ciarán of Saigir with his hosts.
A slaughtered host with splendour, on the feast of Victorinus, will protect us continually and directly [?] to the kingdom of God.
Dear is the godly pair, as is due [?] to our worthy poem: holy Felicitas, Perpetua the foremost.
Senán of Inis Cathaig crucified shameful enmity [?]; Conandil, a victorious champion; bishop Beóáed the warlike.
The death of forty soldiers, with a great host that was radiant, when He raised them up against many, a sun in a black, dark place.
Constantine, fair and lawful, was summoned to the angels, he in whose time was found the angelic tree, the wood of the Lord's cross.
They are companions of our Lord in the kingdom above kingdoms: Librén, Senán the everlasting, Constantine king of Rahan.
To reach his land, for Christ he crucified his body, the hundred-fold victorious organ, Gregory of Rome, very eager [?].
May Mo Chóemóc protect us for the eternal fair protection that will be, and holy Cuangus with prosperity, from Liath Mór: a good pair.
Dionysius the bishop, whose clergy are fair; Christ's namesake, may he protect us: may Salvator free us!
The arrayed [?] dignity of James; Luke, a sea above tresses [?]; with Christ the sons of Nessán from the Island loved converse.
Dear to all except the Devil was Eugenia in the world; Abbán, an angelic golden bush; radiant Fínán the Leper.
The blaze of a splendid sun, the apostle of virgin Ireland, Patrick with the greatness of a thousand, may he be a shelter for our wretchedness!
With a great band of martyrs who were not of many faults, with Tiamda were counted twenty noble soldiers.
Mo Lachtóc with Gregory, the noble champion who is mightiest [?]; Joseph, the noblest name, beautiful foster-father of Jesus.
The death of Polychronius, the holiest bishop: he walked the straightest path, with a great host that was bold.
To the world, a great victory was Benedict, a strong pillar; on the same feast, with a sea of hosts, Énda, famous one of Aran.
The high passion of fair Secundus, in words of life; a strong light of the sea beyond the rampart [?]: Failbe, the glorious one of Iona.
The daughter of Feradach, with a vast host, who is most exalted; from Christ she declares the dignity of my Áedóc, diadem of Scotland.
A splendid, shining pair who strove after unwearied [?] penance: fair Scíre, who loved fasting, and Mochta, faithful and devout.
The crucifixion and conception of Jesus Christ are fittingly on one feast, with diligence, together with the passion of James.
In Latium Mo Chellóc fell, after days [?]; the feast of the everlasting Sinchell of vast Cell Achid.
On the sixth of the Kalends of April, after the releasing of souls, Jesus rose (great tidings!) from the womb of the earth.
May she call us, may she free us beyond pains, may she bless us, may she magnify us: the great Mary Magdalene!
On the feast of the daughter of Baíte, the passion of a great host with modesty, on the feast of a man of virginity, Gregory of Nazianzus.
Name Mo Chuae of Balla, a bag with a dignity of ripe [?] fruit; Colmán of the shining Pool, with the feast of devout Tola.
The glorious [?] cross of Anissius, with a fair clergy that was swiftest [?]; Martha gives victory forever over swarming [?] hosts.
Ambrose, with great purity, ennobles the Kalends of April; it holds the greatest joy, one of the feasts of Mary.
The great host of Amphianus, over whom the Demon was grieved, climbed after a hard battle into the noble, joyful peace.
The host of noble Evagrius, which cast off sorrow with treasures [?]: forty of kings, besides two fair hundreds.
Fair Tigernach the faithful, for Christ he broke every folly; from him burst a stream of wisdom, from Clones of beauty.
On the great feast of Cúla's son, Béccán, whose devotion won victory, Patrick's first baptism was given out in Ireland.
Herenius the bishop, whose thousands are great, was a fair bush with virginity in the Lord's bright vineyard.
Fínán Camm of Cenn Etig, who had great renown; Cainde from Slieve Bloom of the monsters [?] was a champion of Christ.
The death of Enair the martyr; great was the tower of his temple. Cenn Faelad, abbot of Bangor, was not reviled by his community.
The victory of seven innocent holy virgins, known in every house, whose blood is not quenched, on the fair feast of Quadratus.
The cross of Apollonius the priest, borne for fair Christ beyond all wealth; from Ross Eo, a joyful name, royal, very good Cuanna.
May my wealthy Áedóc protect us, for he is a warlike brother; Dúnlang's descendant, though he was made holy, steadfast and [?] (dálach, 'of assemblies'?).
Dálais; dear was Christ's work with holy [?] Cruiche. Julius, bishop, abbot of a people, noble chief of the seat of Peter.
With his first host of good fortune, against the jaws of every mouth [?], Paul the Deacon, fair champion of Christ, has gone; may he [?] us.
The royal bishop Tassach gave Patrick, when he came to him, the body of Christ, the truly strong King, with communion.
A prime flame that does not die out, that overcomes the lusts of desire: Ródán, lamp of Lorrha, was a fair precious stone.
With royal Carissima, whose burial place is famous, the feast of Felix the Deacon comes running [?] to you.
On the feast of Peter the Deacon, Donnán of cold Eigg climbed to victorious martyrdom with his clergy, a fair company.
On the feast of Septimus, noble deacon, Laisrén, a victorious flame, beautiful abbot of Leighlin, is able to comfort us.
Famous Hermogenes, after ending his fight, went to Jesus, a splendid turning, out of the cold of a little body of clay.
With the passion of Herodion, a priest who crucified desire, the feast in Rome, a glorious place, of the saints of all Europe.
To Scotland, in purity, after leaving behind every joy, our brother Máel Ruba went from us with his mother.
May Philip the apostle protect us, who is mightier than every sea; his name is in the Father's mystery, a mouth of broad light.
The lamp of Bishop Ibar, who cut off the head of every heresy. A splendid flame above a shimmering [?] wave: in Ireland Becc died.
The victory of the three innocent boys in the furnace, a famous company; the passion of George, a victorious sun, with thirty great thousands.
Noble Mark in Egypt, who deserves no word of neglect; a rod of gold, a huge bar of metal [?]: Macc Caille, the great bishop.
Cyril, a fair captive, suffered a field of spear-points. He sang praise to Christ with a vast host around him.
Angels brought him out of prisons, though he had gone into them: noble Alexander, abbot of Rome, the believer.
Christopher, with Crónán of Roscrea, steadfastly. On their feast a great host of soldiers went, without arrogance, to martyrdom.
The martyrdom of Germanus the priest — Christ, great was his coming! Coningen, a fair pillar, shares the same festival with Fiachnae.
They close April's company, for he who reckons them is diligent: Rónán of Líathros Uanni, and in Rome the crucifixion of Quirinus [?Cyrinus].
The Kalends of May, Neth Chóeme [?]: the birth of Philip, the most eminent. There the beautiful preaching of Jesus begins, the most noble.
The departure of Saturninus to Christ took place, together with the death, after long sighing, of Nechtan, Patrick's fosterling.
The first finding of the wood of Christ's cross, with many virtues; the death of Conláed of fair age; the great feast of Mary the Virgin.
On the passion of Antherus, fair Mo Chuae departed, the son of famous Cummíne, on the feast of Silvanus the deacon.
The deacon Eutimus, with Hilary, went beyond pains on the day of the feast that raised them to the Lord.
The man who wrote the fair tidings of crucified Christ without stint is honoured with princes [?]: the great birth of glorified Matthew.
Mo Chúaróc with Breccán, two champions, the purest, loved Christ the most dear, in Echdruim of Daire.
Victor and Maximus came to Christ. For love of the King whom they loved, they poured out their blood.
The great manifestation of Michael to the world was a proven tale; the passion of fair, beloved Cyril; famous Bishop Sanctán.
In the peaceful kingdom of the altar, where the sound of every temple is heard, may he protect us: Comgall of the hosts, the victorious one of Bangor.
The triumph of Job, not to be forgotten, was renowned to the King of the clouds; Mo Chrítóc of the fair household, and Cormac the priest.
Cyriacus, crucified with three hundred, comes to us; Ailithir, a lovely name, with holy Erc Nascae.
The holy company of Taracus and Probus followed in their paths: six and six hundred, after lasting, bitter crucifixions.
Corona and Victor with their company, without failing [?], on the same festival, a lasting sea [?]; the fair feast of Carthach of Rahan.
The grace of the sevenfold Spirit blessed a bright-mouthed company: Tiamdae, rich Sárán, the feast of mighty Duiblitir.
The summoning of Brendan of Clonfert into the eternal, victorious kingdom; the holy death of pious Carnech; the splendid feast of Úa Súanaig.
The host of Adrian, Victor and Basilla: with no feeble portion [?], they came to rest on the height of the bright kingdom.
The feast of Mark, who was well exalted [?]; my great, treasured Áedóc; Mo Domnóc, a victorious diadem; the feast of Bran Becc of Cláine.
The pure companies of Urban: desires did not wound them. Their souls are bright through the drops of their blood.
The great blood of Marcellus went under the earth in death [?]. On the same festival, Gervasius and Protasius are invoked in prayer.
Tiamdae, a wonderful martyr; God's great company from Turin [?]; Colmán the Leper, very eager; Barrfind of Druim Cuilinn.
The soul of Rónán the Fair went to starry heaven, together with the fair man of many offspring, Báithéne son of Finnach.
The fair host of Epectitus, the boldest and firmest: after suffering at the hands of persecutors, it was welcomed by angels.
Augustine the bishop; Hermes, great abbot of a thousand; Colmán, a beloved pillar; Aidbe, the lordly one of Tír.
The feast of John comes to you, a beloved, virginal pillar; Dionysius of sure boldness; Dúnchad of cold Iona.
The just reception [into heaven] of Colmán of Stelland: proclaim it without [?]. Béccán loved cross-vigils; his dwelling was in Cluain Aird.
Aculius the priest with his clergy, who are holy: his blood was shed upon the fields before every generation [?].
May he protect us on the way to the angels, a beloved, prosperous throng: Germanus, sun of our elders, foster-father of Patrick of Armagh.
The great host of Pollio, may they protect us on the way to starry heaven! together with Cumman of pure goodness, the beloved daughter of Allén.
The holy apostle of our Lord, in the depths of wisdom: the birth of Thomas, without refusal; the passion of Eutychius, without fear.
The suffering of Chrysogonus, with the passion of Petronella, in the month of May, with a host of thousands: two chief feasts that protect us.
Raise your mind [?]: the feast of Thecla, whose first singing is owed by us, with a vast and noble host, at the front [?] of the Kalends of June.
Erasmus the bishop, a splendid flame with the heat of power, brought to Christ a victorious clergy: three hundred praiseworthy soldiers [or thousands] [?].
A soldier of Christ in the land of Ireland, a lofty name across the wave of the sea: Kevin, holy, fair champion, in the Glen of the Two Broad Lakes.
Apollinaris went straight to God's kingdom with his virginal clergy, together with the translation of Martin.
The martyrdom of Marcian magnified many victories: some of them great men, of good lineage; others pure virgins.
The perfect passion of Amantius, a great deed if you would weigh it [?]; Mael Aithgin of pure goodness went beneath the earth's sod [?].
The summoning of Paul the martyr after a great deed done with strength; the feast of Columb, without pride, the great one of the Moccu Artai.
The reception of holy Job after victory and a bright battle; the feast of Medrán of great consolation; the feast of Murchú of great grace.
May they protect us on the way to the eternal kingdom, in an ever-living, radiant light: Báethíne, lofty and angelic; Colum Cille, shining like a candle.
They meet on one path, without delay [?] for whoever has found them: the chief feast of Mark, an illustrious diadem, with the victorious feast of Barnabas.
Basilla the victorious was carried from us in joy; the feast of holy Mac Táil, with the passion of Fortunatus.
The feast of pious Cóemán, who is named Sanct-Lethan; Torannán, enduring and mighty [?], across the broad, ship-laden sea.
With lively Bartholomew (they are dull who have not heard it), Mac Nisse, the holy one of Cluain, went from us to the kings.
Both meet on one feast-day, a throng like the sea [?]: Nem moccu Birn the mighty, with Benedict the victorious.
A blessing on the champion who loved Christ with true generosity: with him went a host with great valour, Vitus, the wondrous boy.
My champion is Quiricus, before whom a host of good people bowed down; no path or likeness to him has been found among the sons of the world.
The golden bush over the lands, the splendid sun above the peoples, the champion of kings, the strong brother, the fair soldier, Moling Luachra.
With Báithín, fair and prosperous, Furudrán with keenness, the sons of Móinán with virginity, from bright Land Léri.
Their blood flowed over the fields before hosts, with violence: dear to the King were Gervasius and Protasius.
The passion of Paul and of Cyriacus, with that great company; Fáelán with that victory, that splendid Dumb One.
Famous Ainle with his hosts, against whom the sea full of beasts surged; Cormac, who was a fair cleric, the brilliant grandson of Liathán.
With James son of Alphaeus, twice eight hundred, a bright company; the feast of a man who did not love bodily vice, mighty Crónán of Ferns.
The commemoration of Mo Choe: there is nothing that [?] us; the famous, happy abbot from Óendruimm, may he [save?] us!
The royal birth of John the Baptist, if you have studied it diligently, with the translation, without reproach, of John the youth to Ephesus.
The feast of Sinchell, the feast of Telle, who were the exalted ones of Ireland; with Mo Luóc, pure and bright, the sun of Lismore in Scotland.
Vast is their suffering, their passion which [?] them: the fair sun Gallicanus, John and Paul.
Proved through martyrdom that was great, heavy, and fierce were seven true brothers of the city in broad, wide Rome.
In great Leccan of Meath, Crummíne with splendour; on the same festival, with diligence, the fair passion of Fabian.
The feast of Paul and Peter, with the vastness of their renown; the din of battle has not surpassed them, a feast on the forefront of the world.
The victory of Saul and Tiamdae, the death of Job of many treasures; they close a fair, gentle [?] lock on the hosting of dear June.
July, on its kalends: the wondrous [feast] of Mary, who magnifies Matthew [?]; the death of Aaron, a venerable abbot; Simon and Thaddeus.
The death of Bishop Eutychius, of Damasus with splendour, the royal passion of Processus, the great torment of Martinian.
The martyrdom of Cirion, O Christ! It is not [the grasping of a tree-trunk?] [?]; the beautiful translation of Thomas; the feast of fervent Dartinne.
The great good dignity of Martin, if you have readily looked upon it, with a hundred wonderful martyrs; Finnbarr of Inis Doimle.
To the martyr Agatho, with his fair united company, Christ granted, smooth peace, his great love with fear.
Mo Ninne of Sliab Cuilinn, who was a fair pillar, won victory, a pledge of purity, the sister of great Mary.
With the great, brilliant hosting of Parmenius, a weighty company, Máel Rúain went up to heaven, the splendid sun of the island of the Gaels.
Broccán the scribe won a noble victory without any stumbling; with Díarmait, a sure flame, the bright sun of Glenn Uissen.
The splendid naming of Onchú: [it comes soon to everyone who calls upon him?] [?]; with Christ, he who loved diligence, fair Garbán of Cenn Sáli.
Proclaim the passion of the seven brothers, for whom Christ's cross was a prison; Cúán; Mark, great the tumult [?]; twelve thousand martyrs.
With the martyrdom of the queen Euphemia, rich in hosts; Benedict, a strong pillar, the devout son of Cú Lóga.
Nazarius, the story of every synod, has gone to the angels; Felix, it was well that he came with his great host, crushing [?].
Sweet is the name, with splendour, of holy Evangelus; together with Mo Shílóc he went to the royal host, into the noble kingdom of peace.
May the bishop protect us: James, who is holiest. We beseech him and entreat him, together with ten infants.
The twelve apostles, who surpass every number: Jesus distributed them to a countless host throughout the seed of Adam.
Every day it will come to you from Christ, if only you ask for it: the prayer, together with a gentle host, of the little boy Mammes.
May their prayers magnify us, of these men and these women, every martyr whom we count, with the host of the Scillitans.
May the hosting of the queen protect us into noble peace, with a great company of seven brothers: the holy Christina.
The holy prayer of Sisinnius: they are feeble unless they look to it. Indeed it comes to you in your need, with a great lively band.
Lively are the maidens: noble, splendid Sabina, the glorious Romula, together with devout Curufin.
The high cross of Elias the martyr exalted [?] a churchyard full of graves; with a shapely band of maidens, the passion of fortunate Praxedes.
The fair offspring Mary Magdalene, diadem of every fortress; the passion of noble Apollinaris; Mo Bíu of Inis Cúscraid.
With the passion of Vincent a swarm went to Christ: in Rome (it was the course of elders) eighteen thousand good soldiers.
If it is fitting for you, O Ireland, a champion of battle will come to help you: you have the head of a hundred thousand, Declan of Ardmore.
Mo Cholmóc, Mo Shilóc, together with Nessán, if you would dare: James without disgrace, the death of the brother of John.
In the passion of Jovian, with his fair clergy of pure gold; the transfiguration of Jesus after twilight [?] on Mount Tabor.
The death of Simeon the monk (he was a great sun to the earth), with the passion of a beloved host in high, vast Antioch.
Vast is their help, with their bright, candle-like host: Theophilus, an angelic tower of gold, and radiant Pantaleon.
Lupus and Simplicius, bishops without any unworthy share; Prosper with a complete clergy, the royal stars.
Besides singing the law of Christ, they studied it with its mysteries; no fault was found with their host: Abdon and Sennen.
The host of July, as great as a thousand: a high pillar protects them, a splendid bishop of Ireland, Colmán son of Dar Áne.
On the calends of August great power arrived: with the feast of the sons of the Maccabees, eighty great thousands.
With that great mother Theodota, that vow [?]; with that victory went those three tender little sons.
The metropolis of John [?], a beloved feast with splendour; in an assembly with holiness, the noble body of Stephen.
Let him be joyful after reaching the kingdom (great is my hope in him): the holy, royal champion Mo Lua son of Óche.
The splendid passion of Herentius [?] deserves a fair invocation [?], together with holy Oswald of prayer, high-king of the noble Saxons.
Sixtus, bishop of Rome, carried up a floating swarm [of souls], together with Mo Chua, victorious pillar, from Clondalkin of the assemblies.
Count five above three fifties of years (a power that has served us): seven great men without blemish slept in Ephesus.
The feast of Beóán son of Nessán, great [?]. It is no petition of a wretch [?]: Colmán, the beautiful bishop, from Inishbofin.
Mark the passion of Antony and of Firmus's very strong household. In Achad Cáin is buried Nath Í, a faithful priest.
The full cross of Lawrence the deacon was hard on his poor body; with a whole, noble, fair-coloured host comes fair Bláán of Cenn Garad.
Pray to Airerán of wisdom, whose fame is not hidden, together with pure Valerian and Tiburtius, strong and prudent.
The calling of Lasrén of great, glorified Inis Muiredaig, with a holy company that does not die; the feast of famous Ségéne.
Hippolytus the martyr: his death was a marvel. With a vast, noble host comes Mo Mo-Áedóc, diadem of the Irish.
With the calling of Fortunatus across the sea of the ship-filled ocean, the son of the craftsman, a fair captive [?]: the feast of Fachtna son of Mongach.
On the great feast of the departure of the true mother of our Father, with a host of kings, a splendid convent [?]: Fer Dá Chrích, a fair city [?].
With the cross of Adrion, with a company that did not love [?], the birth of Mary, diadem of pure strength, holy mother of my royal Son.
Mammes the martyr suffered great pain on a hard cross; with a fair, guiltless company comes the death of Temnén the monk.
Mac Cresséni, Mo-Ernóc, magnified the Lord of our band; a man of grace for our help was Daig, great and good, son of Cairell.
The cross of the martyr Magnus, with a company with the victory of blossom; Mochta the great, good peace [?]; Énán of Druim Ráthe.
Dioscorus, the most manly champion, suffered for Christ; Pamphilus, a most wondrous flame, with a great bright host.
On the feast of Vincent, pray to the eloquent bishop Senach of great Clonard to help your soul.
Make a petition to Timothy, disciple of Paul, with splendour; with holiness, pray to the youths of the holy Emilianus.
With the passion of Fortunatus (a battle-host went about it) on one festival, praise of the world, is the feast of Eógan of Ard Sratha.
With the array of Zenobius's host (it is a tale well heard) comes Old Patrick, champion of battle, fair tutor of our sage [?].
The tale of his passion has spread on every side to the streaming sea: victorious Bartholomew, who was stretched on a great cross.
The victory of Abundius the martyr: rise up to celebrate it! With a radiant host he climbed to heaven after tribulation.
The company of the pure martyr, fair Rufinus, with melody: to the holy King of the clouds [?] he went through a field of spear-points [?].
May Cyriacus protect us with his fair, catholic company. Hermes, the illustrious one from Africa, suffered with great groaning.
Proclaim the passion of John the Baptist, always diligently, with nine hundred in virginity, at the taking up of Elijah.
Splendid is the perfect Agapa, who is a sun to the saints; she won victory above victories with her noble sisters.
Aedán, the bright sun of praised Inis Medcoit (Lindisfarne), together with Paulinus of the widows [?], adorns the end of August.
On the calends of September, Cecilia with her uprightness, with four hundred in perfection and twenty-three thousand.
Praise Theodota with Senán; they are noble with fair Christ. Their victory with their clergy: they are precious.
Colmán of Druim Ferta, Longarad, a sun of beauty [?], Mac Nisse of Condere the great, with thousands.
In the great kingdom without sorrow [?] the little ones are blooming; his little boys keep a great feast around Ultan of Ard Breccáin.
Count Brecc-búaid as well. Called from Ireland was holy Eolang of Achad Bó, a fair pillar, a triumph of diligence.
Luscai, with Mac Cuilinn, a fair pair that he shares out [?]; the feast of Scéth is here with us, and that of Columb of bright Ros Glanda.
The pure passion of Senotus, who are lights: kneel! The host of Anastasius: pray to them, with the multitude of their miracles.
Mary is commemorated; you are not dead on a scanty portion [?]. Then come Tiamdae and three hundred martyrs.
A great festival that fills the lands and rocks swift ships: the Son of the Carpenter, above kings, the fair feast of Ciarán of Clonmacnoise.
A pillar of red gold with purity, who brought law over this sea [?], a sage through whom Ireland is at peace [?]: Finnbarr of Mag Bili.
The passion of Protus and Hyacinth, which came with much suffering [?]; Sillán, the psalm of every sick person, is sung sweetly in Imlech.
Celebrate the feast of Ailbe, with bright, swimming Fled [?], on the feast of shining Laisrén of crowded Daiminis.
Proclaim twenty-two martyrs of great holiness, with the champion of battle, Dagán of Inber Dóile.
The feast of Cóemán Brecc falls to you, with a fragrant pair: the holy passion of great Cyprian and the fair passion of Cornelius.
With the consecration of the basilica of Mary, a strong wall, Cyrinus, without pride, went with a great host of martyrs.
A great trio, not a sad one: Mo Ninn, praised by every mouth, blessed Laisrén of Iona, and great Laisrén of Mena.
Euphemia, without unworthiness: tell her passion at the year's turn [?]. Recount Broccán of Ros Tuirc, with the very good feast of Riagail.
Seven hundred blooming soldiers reached heaven, along with the fair birth, without unworthiness, of Énán of Druim Ráthe.
With a multitude of the renowned, Januarius, precious and gentle, has reached Christ with his great royal host: a dear commemoration.
Let us beseech the virgins who have watched over our gatherings [?], the queen of Dar Óma [?] with her host: may she protect us!
May the chief with his great host protect us in the high, gleaming station: the bright sun of lovely colour, Matthew, a strong wall [?].
Pantaleon and Mauricius: how many are their great hosts? A fair host of six hundred warriors on top of twelve thousand.
To Adamnán of Iona, whose host is shining, noble Jesus has granted the lasting freedom of the women of the Gaels.
The conception of noble John the Baptist is the greatest of tidings: except Jesus, he is the most wonderful of humans ever born.
With the clergy of Eusebius you have made every great feast noble, together with the festival of the loving man, the feast of Barre of Cork.
Colmán of Lann Elo, with virginity and lofty learning, so that he is (a splendid cry) the great John of the sons of Ireland.
Our two keen champions of the heart, their cross was no [?]; may they protect us, for they are our own: Cosmas and Damian.
The two bright Findias are entreated for every help; the great company of humble Marcellus; Iunaill [?] with the festival of Lobar.
With the fight against the hostile dragon, for Michael, strong and victorious: the bright-sided soldier with his host will destroy the wrathful Antichrist.
September, after its swarms [?], they would seek [?]: a sound, eloquent, everlasting sage, fair Jerome of Bethlehem.
The victory of Priscus, the passion of Lucas [?], the festival of Germanus, a sun of songs, the feast of the noble holy relics at the beginning of October.
Eleutherius the martyr, his feast is honored [?] on one line with the passion of Eusebius.
The noble birth of Mark in Egypt, to be proclaimed by every mouth. Candida, a happy sun; the fair birth of Colmán of Elo.
Entreat Bishop Marcellus, with the greatness of his might, together with the passion of the virgin, bright-limbed Baluína.
A fragment of the precious stone, with a host of wonderful martyrs: Sínech, daughter of Fergna, of Cruachu of Mag Abnae.
Lucell, abbot of Clúain, with mighty Báithíne; Fer Dá Chrích, a victorious pillar; the feast of splendid Bishop Lugaid.
With Matthew, Bishop Mark, who struck down a host [?] with few; with a fair clergy with melody, the feast of Cellach with radiance.
A flock of maidens in virginity gave up their strength, with splendor, for the everlasting dwelling of the kingdom, together with the bright passion of Faustinus.
On the feast of Eusebius a vast host of kings went up along the paths: three hundred and fifty.
Three hundred and thirty, with the fair man without stealth: fair Fintan, root of a kindred, pillar of Druim Ingaird.
Splendid is the number of the three whom we name: Fortchern, radiant Lommán, Cainnech of the Moccu Dálann.
Proclaim Fíacc and Fiachra [?]; great is that treasure. Mo Bí (strong is their victory), that fair flat-faced one.
Comgan and Marcellus, with the breadth of their flood [?]; the pure young queen, the feast of fair Findsech.
The feast of Bishop Callistus, declare it on one line with the virginal passion of Bishop Paulinus.
The chief passion of the Moors [?] was heard throughout the populous world; they suffered much [?] after bitter prisons of fetters.
Though three fair hundreds and forty belong to that victory, Riaguil is the surety of their course, and Colmán of Cell Rúaid.
The great martyr, heavenly Nicodemus, suffered with his clergy, a fair birth, a champion who drove out demons.
Certain it is that, with the passion of Philip the chief martyr who has increased us, Christ gave fair help to Tryphonia the faster.
May Auster, who rose up through torments, be a help to us; may the host of Susi protect us and free us from pains!
The passion of Eutaicc [?] with Fintan Máel Dub, great is their acclaim; a fair sun at that mountain, of that noble Eóganacht.
A splendid flame with a father's ardour is Fintan, true proven gold, son of Telchán, a mighty faster, a faithful, crucified soldier of battle.
The cross of Philip the bishop, with whom a host was slain [?] diligently; Matthew, diadem of every kingdom, with the passion of Eusebius.
The contest of Longinus, most zealous [?] for the royal kingdom: he pierced (a most noble deed) the beautiful side of Jesus.
The noble proclamation of Severus is best for you, if you would know it: he raised to noble heaven forty Christians.
Four tens and two fifties come to us with Maximus; Christ, with the feast of a man of understanding, great Laisrén son of Nasca.
Nassad, Beóán, Mellán, in whatever way I weave them [?]: dear the fitting four, the feast of the daughters of Mac Íair.
Erc of great Domnach, rich in treasures; Abbán, a fair abbot with clergy; Odrán, a noble swimming [?] chief; Colmán, grandson of Fiachra.
Wide is their assembly, Babylon is their burial-place: Thaddeus and Simon, very great is their host.
May the host of Quintus, with great ardour, protect us from every danger: they won victory after forgiveness, with Taimthenne's [?] tálgud [?].
Two hundred and sixty whole on one feast-day, a sea of victorious ones [?]; Ernach the virgin, a lofty pillar; Colmán moccu Gúalae.
Quintinus, fair, crucified; Fáelán with a great reaping-band [?]: they close, with a host of fathers, lofty October's end.
Lonán, Colmán, Crónán, with their bright, sunny clergy; the hosts of Hilary, steadfast in assembly, ennoble stormy Samain.
The elder of the apostles of our land, Patrick, the chief pillar, gave a blessing of victory upon Bishop Erc of Slane.
Proclaim Hilary across the great sea; Murdebar, diadem of a synod; the fair feast of Corcu Nutain, with the feast of Cóemán of Enach.
A dear sun without sudden ending, with a great company without timidity, Perpetua without unworthiness, the chief spouse of Peter.
The passion of renowned Domninus, before whom the sons of men bow; full of the grace of God was Colmán of Glenn Delmaicc.
Though men cast them down through martyrdom with splendour, the mysterious kingdom of heaven was attained by the company [?] of Hadrian.
The vast throng of Eusebius, though grievous its path, found (a very mighty choice) a great land in the plain of heaven.
To heaven goes the cry of Claudinus: a fair company went without reproach, with the feast that fills the peoples, of Barrfind, great son of Áed.
Donatus and Damian were not weak [?] wretches: on the same feast-day, with gladness, the feast of Sinech with richness.
Áed son of Brecc of the royal line, little but that he was greater [?] in death; high in the great kingdom is the chief of the race of Conn of the Hundred Battles.
Cairbre of Cúl Rathin, royal grace across the great sea; Saint Martin, noble likeness, mountain of gold of the western world.
Bestowed with wisdom and skill, with a wealth of [?], on my Cummaine, a fair soldier: the fair son of Fiachna, Fota.
On a withe [?] died Eutaicc [?] the martyr. If you have thought about it, before the high Christmas, abstinence [?] marks the beginning of Lent.
Clement and Colmán: celebrate their feasts. For the birth of Christ, begin [?] diligence with chastity.
With the passion of Secundus, with a host of every colour: if Lent is upon you, begin the struggle of your battle.
The company of Augustine, the best of bishops, who loved fasting. Forty fair, devout ones overcame many grievous sicknesses.
Celebrate the feast of Thecla; she fell after victory. Buadbeó, an enduring, strong city, together with fair Duilech of Clogher.
Fair is the consecration of the church of Peter and of chief Paul. Berach's son, with virginity, and the bright feast of kingly Rónán.
Tell of the consecration of the basilica of John, a son without disgrace. Forty [?] went with Maximus, a great champion.
Entreat Esca, with Fróechán, against strong-mouthed monsters [?]. With the passion, with its mysteries, of the host of Bassus beneath the clouds.
A holy pair went to Christ with the birth of Clement: the son of Comman from Aran, and the son of Congraid from Ireland.
After suffering in martyrdom (O Mary!), a flashing light, fair, candle-bright Cecilia went to the angelic royal Son.
The fair passion of Clement among the waves of the sea. His shrine is venerated beneath the waves of the wide sea.
With Cianán of Duleek, a fair pair for our help [?]: the very eager [?] son of Lénéne, together with Colmán of Dub Cuilinn.
With John Cassian, of the very fair tonsure, Findchú of Brí Gobann went from the Cross [?], a fair domain.
Entreat a sure, assembling pair with a fair, victorious people: Banbán, a glowing flame of gold, and Bishop Siricius, streaming [with grace].
A stream of wisdom with splendour, Sechnall, a diadem over princes, sang (noble the gain) the praise of Patrick of Armagh.
The chief triad, not transient, of Trophimus without [?]: the sons of Bochra (lasting victory!) from smooth Achad Rathin.
The royal feast of Brendan of Birr, toward whom diligent throngs [?] pour forth. He was a fair diadem of great pride, the fair head of the prophets of Ireland.
Andrew, who is boldest toward the cross, a step that is most perfect, brings November to its close over the hosts, I declare.
Proclaim the Calends of December: Candida, fair [?]; the hardy passion of Pancras; the holy feast of Nessán of Ulster.
The great passion of Parmenius after bitter perils of hunger. Entreat, with a multitude of martyrs, Máel Odrán, great and exalted.
The high martyrdom of Heraclius with his company, the truly steadfast one. Mac Óige, with perfection, the pilot of wonderful Lismore.
Merobus and Claudicus, with the vastness of their array. The generous Fer Dá Lethe was one of our noble elders.
The commemoration of Justin the bishop, with splendour; of Amantius, Crispinus, Umbanus and Philadius.
The feast of Gobbán (a shout of thousands), with a company of great martyrdom, an angelic wall, an abbot of virginity; the flashing sons of Lán.
The passion of Polycarp with his noble, abundant clergy; from rich Monasterboice, the feast of fair, victorious Buite.
The victory of humble Ichtbrichtán, who came across the great sea; he sang vigils to Christ in a little coracle, without sleep.
Two daughters of Ailill, who are not hidden, fell asleep [died]. Fair is the host of their day, the two suns of eastern Liffey.
With two fifties of virgins and a full thirty exactly, the festival of Capitolinus, the feast of my bold Dímóc.
Damasus, with my Senóc of northern Mugna, a broad plain; the feast of my Elteóc, a holy warrior, with a strong host across the sea.
A tower of gold over every wide plain, who will rightly take up my soul's cause [?]: fair Finnian, a beloved root, of great Clonard.
On a dear, crowded day they have come in the greatness of a thousand: Báethán of faithful Cluain, and fasting Columba of Tír [Terryglass].
May he summon us to the royal kingdom, the king who carried off [?] our sister: Drusus with his three, a holy, just champion who overthrows [the enemy].
The summoning of fortunate Faustus with the fair clergy of his church, with the feast of Flann, a festive ruler [?], the lasting successor [abbot] of Bangor.
The fair victory of Valentinus with a fair clergy you have proclaimed [?]; the feast of most fervent Mo Beóóc of candle-bright Ard Cainrois.
May the host of Victor protect us, after the victory of their deed of valour, until we reach, a splendid joy, Jesus, the great Son of Mary.
Great sun of these clans, Magniu, good is this his diadem; Diucaill, swift this their time [?]: may they be welcoming to me.
May she be welcoming to my soul with the vastness of her host, the fair, pure manna of God of the elements, Samthann of Clonbroney!
Mighty, after devotion, was a great host whom I mention, who were given up [?] from us by hundreds in the company of Ignatius.
The prayer of holy Thomas we invoke before [?]; his death in India, across the regions [?], was a wondrous [?] tale.
May the prayer of Tua of Itharnasc, who does not speak, protect us, with bright Éimíne from the bank of the silent Barrow.
The passion of eight hundred fair martyrs, with sixty of noble rank [?], with my Themnióc of the royal folk, of truly good Clonfert.
The service of Lucianus, with my fair Chua [?], son of Lonán, who came to us on the night before Christmas.
At the great Christmas, a marvel, Christ was born of fair, pure Mary, destroying darkness: the bright king of Adam's seed.
We invoke for our protection Mo Chommóc with splendour, and the fair sun who warms thousands, the bright name of Stephen.
The peaceful sleep of John in Ephesus, a splendid city; and his brother, whom I exalt, with dignified James.
Renowned is the eternal cry, beyond every fair band of reapers, sung on high to their father, of the little boys from Bethlehem.
Their help will be powerful at every hour we call on it: Victor with a famous host, with wise Airerán.
Violence in prison tormented the great host of Mansuetus; with Ailbe of virginity we shall reach his feast.
Lochán and Énda, Silvester of noble talent: on his feast, no feeble [?] leap, let us advance a step onto the calends.
From one kalend to the next we have carried out our quest: O Jesus, in true goodness, may you possess your year!
The companies of each single day, which we have listed above, we have [?] set out in order, from the start of January to the start of January.
Our strength was weak in a lowly little body, but something nobler drew us on: the high love of Jesus.
The patriarchs and prophets, though they were companions of Christ, their feasts are not fully known among men.
But it is known that no soul from this lasting world has reached the high heaven of this King except on one of these feast days.
A full company each day into the vessel of the glorious kingdom, after victory and triumph, has come to serve us!
To heaven they went each day out of the wrath [?]. It is no lie, though they were more than thousands of thousands.
Of those great thousands, of that mighty, lasting sea, we have brought from that number only the kings of those hosts.
A fair hosting every day, of vast power: from every side, across the peoples, they come to me with kings.
O holy King, I pray to you, for after weariness I have reckoned them: may I live forever in your paradise with the host I have reckoned!
The kingly company I have reckoned is a mouthful from a great sea. May each of them, with a devout company, be helping me!
May they all raise me up to my King, whose kingdoms are reckoned [?]; may my elders protect me, each with the company of his day.
The company I welcome, together with everyone I have loved: may they protect me with my band, head, mind and body with soul.
Every soul that has reached heaven, a harder course [?], will reach what is nobler [?]. May the blessing of Jesus be on us.
May all of them help us, together with the host they go to; may they sanctify us and exalt us before the high King whom they serve.
May the full blessing of this King with his fair hosts be over your gatherings, upon Máel Ruain, before all people!
May my fosterer bring me to fair Christ, dear beyond all [?], with his blessing in purity, with the fervour of his heart.
O Christ, may I be raised up, below and above, out of every disgrace; meet my sloth with tenderness, instead of your severity [?].
The writing we have made about the princes of Christ is right [?]: because we have searched through books, it holds much profit.
It is a profit to students if it is a breastplate of devotion; it serves [?] every generation for proclaiming the feasts.
Though they are sages who read it, its pools are broad; there is much high beauty in it, whose verses they delight in [?].
The King of heaven with his angels, whose fame we do not hide, and every martyr we list came to make it.
It was not ease [?] that made the diligent, brilliant little book, but the help of the angelic King, fair, shining little Jesus.
A fair assembly came to me in the middle of my house to correct it in your presence according to the rule of the King of heaven.
It was not wealth [?] that achieved it, and it is a sin for us to boast [?] of it: every glorious, pure saint made its chapters.
The order of the chapters: if anyone should disturb it, I declare before this company that it is a loss to this host.
The host whom the little book has carefully set in order: so that they may be heard in purity, they have fixed their feasts.
A calendar that I have searched out far and near; I made it with goodwill, and I have given it to the saints.
They have given their blessing to everyone who recites it; they will come to attend him at the time when he dies.
With the life of his soul in the kingdom of the bright sun, after it has been carried past torments to the fortress of the seven heavens.
It is not out of forgetfulness or neglect of anyone who has not been listed. It is for brevity of speech: I have fitted it to the rules of metre.
Even if I had seven tongues in my mouth, those of a wise and learned sage, I would be counting them until Doom, a task greater than any speech.
The carefully made little book is not excess or [?], but a commemoration of pure saints, set in order with skill.
Though our little book is smooth and its joints are nimble, it was not wooing or pride that gathered a great part of it.
The vast portion of Ambrose, the Sensus of Hilary set out carefully, the Antigraph of Jerome, the martyrology of Eusebius.
A gathering of the books of Ireland, [?], we have collected their multitude: the calendar of the men of the Gaels.
I promise without blushing: though you should go even into graves, you will not find among any people a calendar that is more correct.
Keeping its song without error is a citadel; it is a strong wall without deceit against men and against demons.
Toward God it is a prayer; against the Devil it is a defence [?]. It is a psalm that declares great might; it is a truly correct calendar.
Everyone who delights in this noble, enduring song: this host will protect him in the everlasting kingdom of this King.
This King's most excellent host, with whom my contention lies: may this cry of mine on their behalf be complete, as my guarantee.
With me as guarantor, and by his guarantee: whoever recites it every day, I promise without falsehood that he will be in the everlasting kingdom.
With the life of his soul with Christ of the fair and mighty kingdom: whoever is accustomed to it until he groans his last, his safe dwelling is not hard to win.
If he recites it purely with clear tears, many wonderful miracles will be done for him.
It is the equivalent of seven masses if a saint reads it; it is the equivalent of three fifties (the whole Psalter) for the free person who recites it.
It is a splendid equivalent of [?] all these feasts; it is the sanctification of his soul and the subduing of his passion.
It is a true making of confession; it is the equivalent of three three-day fasts; for everyone, in whatever place it is sung, it is the prayer of a hundred creeds.
It is a relic, it is communion, it is a canticle upon the psalms; it is a consolation to the devout and an intercession for the dead.
It stirs up devotion even when the heart is hard; it increases his wealth and carries him into the kingdom of heaven.
It is a breastplate around piety against the temptations of demons; it is a [?] of vigil; it is the healer of every plague.
It is a protection in life against the fear of every danger; it is a sanctification of deeds; it is a lengthening of life.
It is a revelation of miracles; it increases every assembly; it bestows the highest love; it is an exaltation of dignities.
It is great fear of the Lord; it is firm divine love; it is the expulsion of demons; it is the summoning of angels.
Wonderful are all the miracles that we declare; a blessing on every person who reads them hereafter.
Should this be what he asks of the Lord in beauty, the worm of the earth will not touch him and his remains will not rot.
His soul, without struggle, will be in heaven with brightness; after him, once it has reached there, the dew of his grave will heal.
At the commemoration of their feast may the force of their prayer protect us: it is no labour in vain; we have enumerated them all.
The royal host I have enumerated, it is near [?] for our [?]; after reckoning their feasts I will enumerate their hosts.
The host of the archangels of heaven around Michael, noble and joyful, with the nine orders of the gracious King of the city of the great King.
The host [?] around Noah across the expanses of the salt sea, companions of the King of the bright kingdom; that was the renewal of the world.
The host of prophets around Isaiah, the fair prophet of song; the patriarchs of prayer, with wondrous Abraham.
The host of apostles around Peter, with the disciples of Jesus; Paul pre-eminent, without fear, the most eminent head of wisdom.
The host of martyrs around Stephen, a golden bush with purity; the anchorites around Paul the Elder; the host of holy virgins around Mary.
The host of the holy bishops of Rome around Peter of the splendid assembly; the bishops of Jerusalem with James of dignity.
The host of bishops in Antioch with Peter, the pre-eminent flame; the bishops of Alexandria with Mark, red-purple and royal.
The host of the saints of Honoratus, the renowned battle-soldier with his hosts; the host of wisdom that was made royal, with victorious Benedict.
The illustrious host of George, not feeble to behold [?]; every boy who went to martyrdom under Herod in Bethlehem.
The host of priests who offered the body of Christ crucified on the cross, to help me every day, with Aaron, the venerable chief.
The host of monks around Anthony, whose courses are mystical; with Martin, warrior of battle; the host of the high saints of the world.
The host of the noble saints of Ireland with Patrick most exalted; Columba holds sway with the hosts of the saints of Scotland.
A last, very great host, which fairly ends [?]: Saint Brigit, after victories, with the virgins of Ireland.
All these hosts, with noble high kings, to help me: a bright-white clergy, a very great army of saints.
Every saint who was, who is, and who will be until Doom, powerfully bestowing [?], in the company of faithful Christ, may they be helping me.
May they be helping me in heaven and on earth, until they come in bands to aid my soul.
My soul, my wounded body, while they are in toil, may the glorious royal host be protecting me.
I have besought the royal host on whom there was [?]; O Jesus, with true prosperity, I beseech them afterwards.
After the enumeration of these hosts, O high King who is not hidden, O Christ whose servant I am, have mercy on me.
Have mercy on me, O royal Prince, according to thy will [?]; O Jesus, I love thee; O great God, I beseech thee.
O great God, I beseech thee, hear this wretched groan of mine, that I may live after this struggle in the everlasting company of this host!
The great host that I recount, which died in every manner: to thee, O Christ most noble, I plead their sufferings.
I plead their truly innocent blood upon the roads; I plead their wounds, their spears through their sides.
I plead their groans, their piercing sighs, to thee, O Christ, for my misery; I plead their purity.
Against the [?] of the world, for great is its weakness, before thee in white raiment I plead their longing.
I plead their spirits in thy royal kingdom with its beauty; to thee, for thou knowest them, I plead their relics.
Whatever petition I pray to thee, that thou refuse it not: over their bright faces I plead their tears.
I plead thy heaven, its firm marvel, from centre to border, with holy hosts of angels.
I plead every offering of thy little body that has been offered with drops, above the clouds, upon holy altars.
I plead the cry of victory above every son of devotion, the little drop of blood of the hour [?] through thine own little side.
Thy humanity, thy divinity, with thy holy, shapely [?] Spirit: I plead thy union with the heavenly Father.
Together with thy saints I plead to thee all that I say, that I may have in thy kingdom whatever I strive for.
Whatever struggle my proud, joyous mind has fallen into, with a blow upon my mindful body, may thy household entreat thee [for me] [?].
Hear, O Jesus, thy weak little exile; I would rather part from the world than remain.
That my wrath [?] may be healed through the granting of my prayer (my friend is not one who refuses), I plead all things to thee.
Hail, O company of heaven! Let one of you raise me up; not being in your company moves me greatly.
Great sorrow moves me here below the heaven of beautiful stars, for your company is good, and your absence weighs heavily on me.
Come to my help, for great is your devotion; heal my heart for the sake of Mary's Son!
Great is the anguish I am in, in a slender little body of sleep [?]; great are my sins; come to my help.
If you have love of God, with its due recounting, there has been here among you, in lowliness, a poor little one for whom it should be done [?].
If you can, a visit: it was time for your coming; here is the least one, a poor wretch of the people of Jesus.
Though it be not unpleasing [?] to you, before the face of this King of the clouds, for I am a wretched poor one without help, [hear] these tears of mine [?].
O host of the saints of the seven heavens, for great is your devotion, save my heart for the sake of Mary's Son.
For the sake of this King, to whom this lament is made, help this wretched poor man out of this anxiety.
Though the brethren may think all these prayers wretched, it is to you, O Christ, that I have now prayed my prayer.
I pray another petition on behalf of the people of the world, O Lord of the kingdom, O King who passes judgments!
Perhaps all this prayer is not pleasing to people; after us, so that there may be no anger, let the prayer be changed [?].
The prayer I have prayed is not out of ill will toward people; I would rather part from the wicked than stay with them.
Let it be heard by you, O Jesus, O Christ whose clients they are [?]; may you grant every prayer of every devout son.
The prayer of every devout son, O Lord, is not in vain; may you grant it to them if their requests are fitting.
If their requests are fitting, O King who rules the earth, may you save their bodies and sanctify their souls.
The soul of every living person is sanctified through you; the seed of Adam, which is most [?], was saved by Jesus.
Save me, O Jesus, my body and my soul, from every evil that comes to me and strikes on the earth.
Save me, O Jesus, O Lord of fair fellowship, as you saved Elijah, along with Enoch, from the world.
Save me, O Jesus, from every evil on earth [?], as you saved Noah son of Lamech from the Flood.
Save me, O Jesus, O King of pure brightness, as you saved Abraham from the hands of the Chaldeans.
Save me, O Jesus, O mysterious, gracious King, as you saved Lot from the sin of the city.
Save me, O Jesus, O noble, wondrous King, as you saved Jonah from the belly of the great whale.
Save me, O Jesus, into your gracious heaven, as you saved Isaac from the hands of his father.
Save me, O Jesus, when you come with your saints, as you saved Thecla from the gathering of the beast.
Save me, O Jesus, you who granted [the request of] your mother [?], as you saved Jacob from the hands of his brother.
Save me, O Jesus, from every evil that [?], as you saved John from the venom of the serpent.
Save me, O Jesus, from hell with its misery, as you saved David from the might of Goliath's sword.
Save me, O Jesus, you who saved all, [as you saved] Susanna with honour after the false accusation against her.
Save me, O Jesus, for the sake of your glory [?], as you saved Nineveh in the time of the plague.
Save me, O Jesus; it is clear to me that you protect [?] me, as you saved the people of Israel from Gilboa.
Save me, O Jesus, O Lord who is most godly [?], as you saved Daniel from the lions' pit.
Free me, O Jesus, O renowned king of good [?] disposition, as you freed Moses from the hand of Pharaoh.
Free me, O Jesus, you have done great miracles, as you freed the youths from the furnace of fire.
Free me, O Jesus, O king of every race, as you freed Tobit from the misery of blindness.
Free me, O Jesus, for the sake of your martyrdom, [as you freed] Paul [and] Peter before kings from the punishment of the prison.
Free me, O Jesus, from the [?] of every plague, as you freed Job from the afflictions of the demon.
Free me, O Jesus, O Christ, may it not be [?], as you freed David from Saul, from his pursuit.
Free me, O Jesus, for the sake of your mother, as you freed Joseph from the hands of his brothers.
Free me, O Jesus, O blessed king, [as you freed] Israel with holiness from the bondage of Egypt.
Free me, O Jesus, for my covenant is with you, as you freed Peter from the waves of the sea.
Free me, O Jesus, from sharp, [?] hell, as you freed John from the vat of fire.
Free me, O Jesus, O king above the princes, as you freed Samson, escaping from the city.
Free me, O Jesus, my soul from every punishment, as you freed Martin from the priest of the idol.
Free me, O Jesus, for the sake of your household, as you freed Patrick from [?] (poisoning?) at Tara.
Free me, O Jesus, for I am your servant, as you freed Kevin from the fall of the mountain.
Free me, O Jesus, your miracles are everlasting; O Lord whom I implore, I await your messengers [?].
When it comes for me to go forth [?], whether at Easter or in Lent, may the royal host that I have commemorated protect me in paradise.
I have commemorated the royal host around the King above the clouds, etc. It ends. Amen.
